GraceRequirements.Annotation: Telos is a semantic-first, agent-native programming framework: systems are Loci composed from semantic extensions, verified by Archetypes and exposed through Packs.
GraceRequirements.Keywords: bun, typescript, effect, semantic model, locus, archetype, packs, agent-native

Goals.Goal: Users define Loci and compose semantic extensions into Locus kinds, with conflicts reported rather than overwritten.
An agent introspects a system through typed queries over the semantic model.
Users operate the calculator proof application through three interfaces: the command line, agent tools and the Web.
An agent discovers and invokes granted capabilities without calling a model provider.
Users verify Loci with Archetype rules that apply according to their composition.
Users see the Loci, relations and rules affected by a change to a capability contract.
Users find every managed code file that no Locus owns.
Readers study the foundation and experiment in the playground on the documentation site.
Maintainers keep the repository free of stale definitions, broken links and unowned artifacts.

Users.User: The owner, who directs the work and makes product and architecture decisions.
Coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) that implement approved Spec Kitty work packages.

Constraints.Constraint: Product changes go through Spec Kitty missions; Spec Kitty owns the change lifecycle, not .grace/changes.
Bun is the only tool: no CI, no Turborepo or Nx, no extra linter or formatter.
No fake tests, placeholder scripts, or checks that verify nothing.
